# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - The end of the third quarter of the year and the start of the fourth quarter were essentially neutral in price terms for gold and silver. Worries over the Greek debt situation continued to rumble, with gold finding some attraction as a safe haven as it rebounded from the strong sell-off. Platinum and palladium were more disappointing and weakened as the Dollar strengthened. With Chinese buyers absent, only industrial buying and a rebound in the Euro helped these two metals regain some of their lost ground. • The most recent Commitment of Traders Report reveals that all four metals again suffered declines in net long speculative interest in New York in the week to the 4th of October. However, the selling was less frenzied than it had been a weak earlier. Investor interest is at low levels by recent historical standards for each of the precious metals and this could provide a buying opportunity should sentiment improve in the short term. • Palladium continued to see heavy ETF selling in the week to the 7th of October. Metal was sold form the platinum ETFs for the fourth consecutive week too as the price fell. Gold saw a small net outflow of metal but sentiment was much improved from a week earlier. Only silver saw an increase in physical ETF holdings with investors apparently sufficiently relaxed about a falling price to continue their buying. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **10 October 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **10 October 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 4 October 2011; ETF data to 7 October 2011.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Margin-driven selling had driven gold down to roughly $1,550 on the 26th of the month but the selling proved to be overdone. As the futures selling slowed, gold bounded back over the $1,600 level on the 26th before charging to $1,670 on the 27th. With the Chinese markets essentially closed, there was, though, no clear direction for the price to move in and, as sentiment ebbed and flowed over the European economic crisis, gold dipped to $1,590 on the 29th of September before climbing to $1,670 again on the 4th despite a strengthening US Dollar. Gold slipped down again on the 4th and the 5th, briefly falling through support at $1,600. It bounced quickly enough, however, climbing again to its current level of just over $1,660. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—October 11** 80

- Net long speculative positions in gold on COMEX fell for the seventh time in the last nine weeks leading up to the 4th of October. However, compared to the enormous decrease of 5.2 million ounces in the previous week, a decline of 355,000 ounces demonstrated a welcome change in sentiment. Larger investors started to trim their short positions, feeling that the price had fallen far enough to provide a buying opportunity. Smaller investors continued to trim their futures positions, however, driving total investor exposure lower. TOCOM saw long liquidation for the second week in a row. Combined positions fell by 450,000 ounces to 21 million ounces, their lowest level since July 2009. - Sentiment was mixed amongst gold ETF investors with the individual funds reporting a mixed performance, some seeing net outflows and others gaining additional investment. Overall, the hefty selling of the previous week slowed to a trickle, with a net 20,000 ounces of metal sold by investors. Total holdings now stand at 67.1 million ounces. 2

Following its $10 fall in the previous week, the price was much more stable, moving in “only” a $2 range for the week. Silver was sold down to $26 on the 26th of September and bounced a remarkable distance to peak at $33.25 on the 27th before settling back closer to $30. On October 5th, the US Dollar started to weaken following the ECB’s decision not to reduce its interest rates. Silver benefited and started to move higher, climbing rather more steadily than has been the case recently to move over the $32 level. - Net silver speculative longs on COMEX fell by 24.5 million ounces in the week to the 4th of October, following their 92.6 million ounce collapse in the previous week, as short positions grew and long positions were closed. In four weeks, investors have reduced their exposure by 154 million ounces, driving total net exposure down to 127 million ounces, the lowest level since late 2008 when the silver price was close to $10 per ounce. Given the decline in speculative interest, silver could now be positioned well for another move upwards once confidence returns. - For a second consecutive week, and the fourth in the last five, ETF investors ignored a falling price and instead added to their silver holdings. 6.6 million ounces were added to global positions, taking them back to 466 million ounces, some 30 million ounces below their peak level but also 30 million ounces above their lows in the middle of the year. #### **Silver Exchange Investment, April 09—October 11** 450 50 Silver price, $/oz

- Platinum fell from above $1,900 in mid-August to under $1,440 on the 5th of October, below breakeven level for part of the platinum mining industry. During this move, the spread between gold and platinum widened with economic concerns providing support for the yellow metal but eroding the supply and demand fundamentals for the white metal. Following platinum’s steep fall to $1,550 on the 26th of September, some rebound was expected and platinum did not disappoint, climbing to $1,585 on the 27th before stopping. However, the economic outlook continued to disappoint and with the Dollar firming and Chinese buyers on holiday, platinum slipped through $1,500 on the 3rd of October and crashed to a low of $1,435

ahead of NYMEX margin increases. As the market chose to hope that the Greek crisis might yet be solved, the Euro then firmed and climbed back through $1,500, pausing briefly to trade currently close to $1,520. - Net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX fell by 78,000 ounces to 1.15 million ounces in the week to the 4th of October, their fourth successive weekly decline. Unsurprisingly, with the price falling below $1,500, some long liquidation was seen but other investors showed more confidence, seeing rising production costs as providing a floor for the platinum price. The market remains mildly bullish although it may be tested by increases in margins on NYMEX in coming days. TOCOM investors were sellers for a third successive week, with long positions falling by 38,000 ounces to 285,000 ounces, less than half their highest level so far this year. - Platinum ETF holdings declined for the fourth successive week leading to the 7th of October. They now stand at 1.49 million ounces, 76,000 ounces below their September highs following selling by North American and European investors. There was, though, some buying interest in one Swiss fund, suggesting that some investors see increasing long term value in the metal at current prices. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **10 October 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 4 October 2011; ETF data to 7 October 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**30-Sep-11**|416,321|512,785|806,293|115,243|153,478|**2,004,120**|| |**07-Oct-11**|410,032|494,128|764,885|124,193|155,677|**1,948,915**|| |**Change**|**-6,289**|**-18,657**|**-41,408**|**8,950**|**2,199**|**-55,205**|| - The palladium price fell sharply from challenging $850 in early August to under $550 at the start of October before recovering a little of this lost ground to trade back over $600 presently. Palladium bounced from its initial drop to $630 as industrial buying emerged, rallying to $655 on the 27th before running out of momentum. It fell back sharply on the 28th, holding $620 but failing to gain ground despite a vital German vote for an expansion of the role of the EFSF in the current crisis. Instead, palladium’s next move was to weaken, dropping through the $600 mark on the 3rd of October despite the announcement of much better than expected

US car sales. The price slumped to a low of $539 on the 5th following fears that Greece might meet an immediate liquidity problem before rebounding as the Dollar weakened following an ECB decision to leave interest rates unchanged. It broke $600 on the 6th and currently sits above that level. • The importance of investment interest to palladium was demonstrated in recent weeks with the price dropping as investors ruthlessly cut their futures positions which fell from a net long of 727,000 ounces in late September to 598,000 ounces in early October. The longer term trend is instructive, with positions having crashed from 1.45 million ounces in early September, reflecting a very substantial worsening of investor sentiment. The current low level of investor involvement may provide a buying opportunity for some but confidence in the short term bullish story for palladium has been badly damaged. - Heavy selling continued in the palladium ETFs in the week to the 7th of October with 55,000 ounces more metal redeemed than purchased. Total holdings slipped to 1.95 million ounces, having last been under the two million ounce level in November 2010. Over a net 300,000 ounces of ETF metal have now been sold by investors since the start of the year although light buying in some funds suggests the emergence of some long-overdue optimism. #### **Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—October 11** 2,000 1,000
